claims.statement: The act's order is accepting before gating before dispatching, and `gate.approve` hard-checks `gate_rev == req.rev` so an approval taken before an amendment is refused as stale — the ordering is enforced by that check, not by etiquette.

In guide mode the five pass-type actions (`proposal.accept`, `gate.approve`, `coordinate.submit`, `verify.submit`, `review.note`) only accept a menu ticket; a directly dispatched one is rejected with `[REJECTED:ACTION]` and the main state does not move.
`*.reject` sits outside the ticket gate on purpose: a rejection produces no pass effect, so it must stay available as the only correction channel.
Only the mod interprets `play.mode`; the host CLI neither reads nor interprets it, which is why `--drive` is an input channel orthogonal to the mode rather than a second decision maker.

A runtime goal run must register `goal.authorization` — trimmed, non-empty, at most 200 characters, no newline — and `review.note` blocks with a narrative line when it is missing; the record proves a sentence was registered, never that the user said it.

Stored truth is two states (`req.<i>.status` = open/done) and the nine phases are derived by the single judge `req_phase()`; `split` / `merged` / `dropped` are `closed_reason` values, and `blocked` / `stale` are display markers, not states.
The accept gate never grants done: approve moves the requirement to `integrating`, and done arrives only with `integration.confirm` carrying a `develop@<sha>` evidence line.

`coordinate.submit`, `verify.submit=true` and `review.note` share one closeout predicate — zero pending proposals, zero running jobs, zero unresolved conflicts, all requirements done including the successors of split/merged rows.

An unarmed batch settle registers `docs.maintenance.due=<batch>` and derives no requirement row; the older `machine.batch-maintenance` text that promised an auto-appended maintenance requirement is stale and the code contradicts it.
The act menu carries one next-step question naming only the actions — accept, gate, dispatch, or close the batch — because the substance of each rule belongs to this page.
